title: Traditional theoretical science fails where irreducibility is present

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Traditional theoretical science fails where irreducibility is present

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Traditional theoretical science, including its use of mathematical formulas, relies on computational reducibility, which is the fundamental reason it has made little progress with systems whose behavior is not quite simple and why it has tended to restrict its domain to reducible phenomena.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: this, I believe, is the fundamental reason that traditional theoretical science has never managed to get far in studying most types of systems whose behavior is not ultimately quite simple.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 12, “The Principle of Computational Equivalence”; section “Computational Irreducibility” (from p. 737), p. 741. Scope: theoretical science and mathematical modeling

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch12-15: not-empirically-resolvable, resolvability 0.27

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Bibliometric and historical records could illustrate associations but cannot resolve the stated fundamental causal explanation. The claim combines a broad interpretation of scientific history with an unfalsifiable counterfactual.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: One could code historical scientific topics by behavioral complexity, modeling approach, and progress, but attributing limited progress fundamentally to irreducibility would require a defensible counterfactual and exclusion of many rival causes.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Rival explanations for scientific progress cannot be cleanly excluded.

The causal and historical terms are undefined.

Selection effects determine what counts as traditional science.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The sentence explains the history of theoretical science rather than stating a variable a dataset records. Bibliographies can show where formulas are common, and the same record fits many other reasons a field stays with tractable problems. No outcome would clearly confirm or refute the stated cause.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: A test would score theoretical domains for behavioral simplicity and for success of closed-form prediction, then isolate computational reducibility as the cause. The claim fixes neither the scores nor a way to separate that cause from other histories of the same fields.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Little progress and not quite simple have no agreed measurement across sciences.

Fundamental reason is a historical cause that instrument limits, taste, and funding also fit.
